title: finding(ci): nothing verifies the seven `@object-ui/*` packages the docs link to are still published — the sweep's 403s never carried that signal, and objectui#8128 stops it pretending to
body:
Found while fixing objectui#8128. Filed because that PR's Lychee exemption comment promises this gap is recorded rather than left implied — this is that record.

Attribution as prose: generated by Claude Code, dev session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, while implementing objectui#8128.

## The gap

`content/docs/**` carries seven links to npm package pages:

```
content/docs/plugins/plugin-ai.mdx:21              @object-ui/plugin-ai
content/docs/plugins/plugin-designer.mdx:21        @object-ui/plugin-designer
content/docs/plugins/plugin-list.mdx:21            @object-ui/plugin-list
content/docs/plugins/plugin-report.mdx:334         @object-ui/plugin-report
content/docs/utilities/create-plugin.mdx:150       @object-ui/create-plugin
content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx:474    @object-ui/data-objectstack
content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx:439              @object-ui/runner
```

**Nothing checks that those packages are still published**, and after objectui#8128 nothing even appears to.

## Why the appearance mattered, and why removing it is the honest move

Before objectui#8128 the weekly `check-links` sweep did check those seven URLs — and rejected all seven, every run, for a month. Measured on scheduled runs 31295178818 (2026-08-09) and 34011606950 (2026-09-06): seven times `403 Forbidden`.

That 403 is npmjs.com's answer to a CI runner, not a verdict about any package. Measured 2026-09-07 against `registry.npmjs.org`, all seven are live at `dist-tags.latest = 17.6.0`. npm returns 404, not 403, for a package that is not there — so the website's answer carried **zero** information either way.

⇒ objectui#8128 excludes `^https://www.npmjs.com/package/` from the sweep. That removes noise, not signal: the sweep never had a true verdict here to lose. But it also makes visible something that was already true — **publication liveness is unchecked**, and it was unchecked while the sweep was red about it too.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT propose

⛔ Not proposing that a gate be built, and not proposing where it would live. This is a coverage reading handed over for triage, not a design.

What is worth recording is that the question has a **working instrument**, which is how the measurement above was taken: `registry.npmjs.org` answers without authentication, without anti-scraping, and returns the actual published versions. Whether that is worth wiring to anything is a decision, not a conclusion of this card.

⚠️ Also worth weighing against it: these are this project's own packages, released from this monorepo by changesets. A package silently disappearing from npm is not a failure mode with a demonstrated instance here, and "startup stage, do not expand scope" applies to gates as much as to features.

Refs: objectui#8128.
